a.text: The snow keeps falling, not heavy, but tacky.
No one knows how long it will keep falling.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Take it and go.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: After I've counted it.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: It's six hundred pounds, what else is there to it? Did you think United Originium Industries would bother to cheat you?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: After I've counted it.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Fine, suit yourself. Might as well.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Two years have passed since the railway stopped operating. You're the last one to sign the settlement.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Fifty-eight, fifty-nine, sixty.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: (Long sigh)

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Finally.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: You signed the agreement, you counted your money. Now go; you don't have anything to do with the company anymore.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: What now? We need to go home too, you know?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I was just thinking.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: About what? Money? You've got all of it, not one pence short.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: About all the things the company promised.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Movie theater, public restrooms, nursery, salt soda in the workshops. Some of them came true, others didn't.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: But I used to think that what was there wouldn't change.

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Whatever you want to think about, do it at home. Get out of here.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: What did the company promise you?

steps.name: Company Representative
steps.text: Just. Get. Out.
Half of the street lamps have gone out due to disrepair, while the rest continue to shine dimly, painting the snowy night over the commercial sector a shade of orange and yellow.
Hold it.
The worker pretends not to hear and keeps walking, until he finds a knife pressed against his abdomen.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: Money.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Don't have any.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: I know you just got a bunch. Hand it over.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: Don't dawdle.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Mechanical division? Which line?

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: How did you know—

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: —Screw that, no questions. Hand over money if you don't want to get hurt.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: What's going on? I could lend you the money, if you're really in a bind.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: You think I didn't try to borrow? Who would lend a sick man money in these times?

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: And did you think I could pay it back, even if you lent it to me?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I can wait—

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: Shut up!

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: I'll count to three. Make up your mind, whether you want your money or your life.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: One... Two...

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: ...Three!

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: I've counted to three! Don't make me do this!

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: My lungs are already rotten! I don't have anything to lose! I'll really do it!

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: Hand the money over!

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: Now!!
Getting no reaction from the worker, the robber presses the knife further forward, cutting open the worker's clothes.
He feels the sensation of cutting open something, and instinctively pulls the knife back, as though shocked by electricity.

steps.name: Robber
steps.text: You—
Before the robber can finish, the worker takes out the flimsy envelope and hands it over his shoulder.

The robber grabs the envelope with trembling hands, looking like a man pardoned on the eve of his execution. By the time the worker turns around, the robber has vanished into the night, along with the money.
Six hundred pounds.
The worker stands there for a while, then walks over to the side of the road. He searches his pockets and finds a cigarette, lighting it with his last match.
He breathes the smoke in deeply and squats down like a drunkard.
A single speck of red light flickers in the night.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I'm back, Rochelle.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Rochelle?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Rochelle Rockwell!

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Where did she go? It's dark, and it's snowing. I've got to look for her—

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: ...Dad.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Why so late?

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: The neighbors were talking...

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: They say you've been robbed.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Is it true?
Her father nods.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: I went to the place they were talking about, but there was no one there.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Who robbed you?

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Thieves from other districts don't bother to come here. It must have been someone from the light industry district.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: He even knew you were getting your settlement money today!

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: I'll catch that thief—

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Let it go, Rochelle.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Let it go?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I had a few words with him. He had no choice.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Dad!

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: We would have lent him the money if he asked properly. He didn't have to rob you!

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: If he was any bolder, you would have—

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: He wouldn't have done it.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: If he had the guts, he would have hit me over the head with a hammer, like that guy a few months ago.
Rochelle shivers.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: He was sick and desperate, and there was no one who would lend him money.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: It was just a moment of weakness. We're all in the same boat. When things get better...

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Will they?

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: They will.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Remember how the boys in the mechanical division made you an operational drone out of spare material for your birthday, a few years ago?

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: Of course I remember.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: It's not just mechanical. We're all family here in the light industry district.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: He'll pay it back.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: What's that? You don't believe your dad?

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: It's not that... Mrs. Clark came to ask for some food in the afternoon because they had ran out.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: She has five kids...

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: I thought you would come back with the settlement money, so I gave them a whole baguette.
The two are silent.
The old house does an adequate enough job of keeping out the wind and cold, though the rattling of the windows is a constant reminder of the snow and wind outside.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: I'll ask Mrs. Clark if they had any leftovers—

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Don't, not with the snowstorm outside.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: I'll go out again tomorrow and see if there are any factories still looking for a stoker. If that doesn't work out, there are always places looking for laborers.

steps.name: Rochelle
steps.text: But your back...

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Who doesn't have some aches and pains around here? I'm one of the lucky ones.

steps.name: Haggard Worker
steps.text: Go to bed. Don't worry about me.
Years Later...

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: I've got another wounded here, Rockrock!

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Coming—Mr. Robertson?!

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: Can you stand, Mr. Robertson?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: Keep an eye on him while I fetch a stretcher, Rockrock.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Did you see any other wounded, Mr. Robertson?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Alright. Don't talk; just hang on. The stretcher will be here soon.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: I found out why the Sarkaz were beating up people in broad daylight.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: What's going on?

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: They imposed a ban on working in the light industry district.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: A ban on working?!

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: All employment relationships outside factories under their control have been banned.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: So they're forcing people into their factories and starving those who don't want to work for them?

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: These people were beaten because the Sarkaz found out they were doing jobs for non-Sarkaz.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: What about the old, the sick, the invalid?

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: Did you think they care?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Those bastards...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: (Deep breath)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Go and check on those whose conditions are less serious. We should have enough medicine, as long as we ration properly.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I'll take care of Mr. Robertson. He's... not in good shape.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: It's time your medicine, Mr. Robertson.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Can you sit up?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson, it's time for your med—

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Hey, you didn't take your meds for the morning!

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: Why... take care of me...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: We care for all the workers of Londinium.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Plus, Dad said we're all family here in the light industry district.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: And you were part of the railway's mechanical divi—
Rockrock did not see Robertson grab his sheets.

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: ...else.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: Someone... else.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Someone else?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Did you want someone else to care for you?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I'll get someone else. But make sure you take your medicine, alright?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Closes eyes)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson!

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Slight nod)

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: How are the injured, Rockrock?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: They're recovering well. We can send them home today.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Once we do that, it'll be time for us to move.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: Robertson has been banging on his bed, by the way.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: He keeps shaking his head, whether it's water, food or medicine that I'm bringing him. It's not toilet stuff either. He's too ill to speak, but he won't stop banging.

steps.name: Self-Salvation Corps Member
steps.text: I think he wants you.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I'll be right there!
Rockrock walks into the tent and sees Robertson still banging on the bedplate weakly.
He only stops once he opens his eyes and sees Rockrock.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: You were asking for me, Mr. Robertson?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: It's alright. I'm here.

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Slaps the bed lightly)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: You want me to sit by your side?
Made from several wooden planks, the makeshift bed would not have fit a bigger man.
Rockrock tries to find a space by the side of the bed, but finds only hard planks.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I'm here, Mr. Robertson.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I heard you've been taking your medicine on time.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: That's good. It'll help you recover...
The sounds that Robertson makes form no coherent words, but the meaning is clear.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: You're right, why talk about that?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: How about we discuss the past?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: When Dad was still around, he used to say that the railway was the lifeblood of the light industry district.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Raw materials come into the district by the railway, into the factories and workshops, and the finished products are transported out of the district to the rest of Londinium and Victoria.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The goods are the blood that flows in the vessels, while railway workers are the... they're the—

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The cells that form the railway.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The cells have to work together for blood to flow unhindered, and the cells in turn get their nutrition from the bloodflow.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I thought about it, and said that the rumbling that the train makes is the pulse of the light industry district.

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Gasps)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Dad thought a bit and said it was a good analogy.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: After that, the trains didn't seem so noisy at all when they rolled by. Instead, they were like my own heartbeat, calming me down when I listened to it.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Rumble, rumble...
Rockrock emulates the sound of a train, while Robertson listens.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Then the factories began shutting down, one by one, and the railway went out of operation...

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Gasps)

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson!?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Sorry, I just kept going...

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Let's talk about happier things.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Look!

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: This is my drone. Its name is Rock-11.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: It's my 11th drone, I started with Rock-1.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The captain assembled it from a motley collection of parts, so it's not as good as what you get in the shops, but I had input in it as well, and the drones have been a big help.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The Sarkaz would've caught us if not for them.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: It's all thanks to you, and Dad's colleagues in the mechanical division.

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Breathes raggedly)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Do you remember how the boys in the mechanical division made a drone for me out of spare parts for my birthday? You were the one who made the core power plant.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I loved it. It couldn't fly very high, but I would hover it at home whenever I had time.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I would look at the spinning rotor, and dream about building bigger and better drones when I grew up.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: That way, dad wouldn't have to watch the boilers night and day, and you wouldn't have to climb up and down all over the place when fixing stuff.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Everyone would live together happily, grabbing a round of beers together after work—

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Mumbles)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Mr. Robertson?
Robertson's coughing interrupts her.
Rockrock sees that his eyes have become wet.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Let's not talk about that! I—
Robertson tries to speak again, but is once again interrupted by violent coughing.
When the coughing finally stops, Robertson raises the hand that he used to bang on the bed and reaches into his shirt.
After some searching, he takes out a small plastic bag filled with money.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Money...?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: For me?

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I can't possibly accept this, Mr. Robertson!

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Slaps the bed)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: No, I really can't.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I could keep it safe until we find your family—

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Shakes head frantically)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: But...
Robertson gazes at Rockrock with pleading eyes, but balks at her determination.
He gives up.
He wants to sigh, but he cannot.
He lets out his breath, and reaches into his shirt again, taking out a stained envelope.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Envelope... a letter?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Sure, I'll deliver it. But the money—

steps.name: Robertson
steps.text: (Bangs on the bed)

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: That's not what you mean?
Rockrock turns the envelope over. The writing on it has long become faded from being soaked in sweat:
Rockwell settlement, 600 pounds.
Rockrock's eyes open wide.
Robertson pulls open the bag with his last remaining strength, spraying the contents all over the floor.
Ten-pound notes, five-pound notes, one-pound notes, even coins.
No settlement money would have been issued this way. It was money saved up, pence after pence.
It was what Robertson got himself beat up by the Sarkaz for.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: ...Mr. Robertson?
There is no response.
As befitting of a laborer, Robertson died silently, having used the last bit of strength in his body.
Another morning comes to the aging light industry district.
The effect of the Sarkaz work ban can be seen in the crowds of workers headed towards the factories in the dim light of dawn.
The Sarkaz sent people to keep an eye on them at first.
But they soon realized that they were like the walking dead, completely silent on their way to work. They never cross the line, even if no one is watching.
The Sarkaz have stopped sending people to monitor the workers, freeing up the manpower to deal with resistance to their rule in other districts.
Poverty and hunger make the best overseers.

steps.name: Silent Worker
steps.text: What's... that?

steps.name: Aging Worker
steps.text: ...A drone?
A patchwork drone flies towards them.
Its bay doors open as it flies over their heads, dropping several bills.

steps.name: Aging Worker
steps.text: Money?
The drone glides over the workers' heads, dropping bills and coins over them like a bizarre snow.
It was equal to the amount of settlement money that a laborer could get after working half his life.
Six hundred pounds.

steps.name: Sarkaz Overseer
steps.text: Search the place!

steps.name: Sarkaz Overseer
steps.text: We got the location of their hideout just this morning! They can't have gotten away so quickly!

steps.name: Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: Sir, there's no one here. They didn't even leave behind anything, except this.

steps.name: Sarkaz Overseer
steps.text: A box of parts? Just on the table like that?

steps.name: Sarkaz Overseer
steps.text: Shoot a bolt into it. See if there's a trap.

steps.name: Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Sarkaz Soldier
steps.text: Sounds like an empty box, sir!

steps.name: Sarkaz Overseer
steps.text: Open it!
The Sarkaz opens the lid of the box carefully.
There is no bomb, no poison, not even a dagger for demonstration.
Inside the box is an old envelope that has been rolled into a ball.
The overseer spreads it out. There is nothing in the envelope; a piece of it has been cut away neatly.
Still unconvinced, the overseer raises it against the dim light and examines it for a while.
Other than the old stains, there are only a few teardrop marks on it.
Years Later...

steps.name: Joyful Worker
steps.text: Huh? It's not the first time you've handed out money?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Yeah, I don't remember how many times I've handed out extra money. It's not like I have any use for it.

steps.name: Joyful Worker
steps.text: Really? Well then, I'll, er, help myself. Thanks.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: You're welcome.

steps.name: Joyful Worker
steps.text: But that's a strange habit. Why did you start doing it? When was the first time you gave someone money?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: The first time?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: It was just after the Self-Salvation Corps was formed. I helped an old colleague of my dad's—
Rockrock looks up at the lead-grey sky, thinking about where to begin.
She catches a glimpse of a new building by the roadside, one that feels rather out of place with the decrepit scenery around it. At the top of the building is a bright neon sign:
'United Originium Industries Londinium Industrial Revival Headquarters'
